title: Gullak Season 5 Is Here. The Mishras Still Live in Your Heart and They Know It.
excerpt: TVF's most beloved family returns on SonyLIV with a new Annu, an astrology side hustle, and the quiet devastation of children who finally leave home.
body:
There is a particular kind of ache that lives in the Indian diaspora. It is the ache of knowing exactly what your mother's kitchen sounds like at 6 PM, of remembering the weight of a steel thali in your hands, of missing an argument you would have given anything to walk away from five years ago. **Gullak** has always understood this ache better than any show on Indian television, and Season 5 — now streaming on **SonyLIV** — proves the Mishras are nowhere close to done breaking your heart in the gentlest way possible.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=yhxf4SYE1gg</youtube>

Seven years. Five seasons. One house in small-town India that somehow contains the entire emotional universe of the Indian middle class. When **TVF** first shot the pilot on a 15-day schedule with almost no budget, nobody — not even the cast — imagined this would become one of the most emotionally resonant shows in Indian streaming history. And yet here we are, with **Filmfare** handing Season 5 a 3.5 out of 5, and the internet collectively weeping over a scene about a father filling out a home loan application.

## What's New This Season

The big change you'll notice immediately: **Anant V. Joshi** steps into the role of Annu Mishra, replacing **Vaibhav Raj Gupta**, who originated the part. It is, on paper, the kind of casting swap that kills shows. In practice, Joshi earns his place with a performance so sincere you stop comparing within the first episode. His Annu has moved out to a rented flat with friends — the first Mishra to leave the nest — and the absence reverberates through every scene like a missing chair at the dinner table.

**Harsh Mayar** returns as Aman, now back from college and hilariously reinvented as an online astrologer dispensing dubious planetary advice to strangers on the internet. It is exactly the kind of side hustle a second-born Mishra would stumble into, and Mayar plays it with the mix of confidence and cluelessness that has always made Aman one of Indian television's most authentic younger brothers.

Meanwhile, **Geetanjali Kulkarni's** Shanti receives an offer concerning her old maternal home — a plotline that will resonate with anyone whose family has ever faced the gut-wrenching question of what to do with the house you grew up in. And **Jameel Khan's** Santosh, ever the quietly ambitious patriarch, has set his sights on purchasing a new home and securing a bank loan to make it happen. The irony of a man chasing a bigger house while his children are busy leaving the current one is not lost on the show.

And then there is **Sunita Rajwar** as Bittu Ki Mummy, who discovers social media activism and feminism with the enthusiasm of someone who just learned the word "patriarchy" and intends to use it in every sentence. Rajwar steals scenes with the ease of someone who has been doing it for five seasons.

> "Not even in my wildest dreams did I think this would go on to become a cult show. This has been a roller coaster ride completely, right from 2018-19 to 2026, and I feel blessed and proud to be a part of this show." — Jameel Khan

## Why the Diaspora Needs This Show

Here is the thing about Gullak that no other Indian show replicates: it makes the ordinary feel sacred. There are no gunfights. No courtroom twists. No lovers separated by fate or caste or a conveniently placed amnesia diagnosis. There is just a family sitting in a room, talking about money and meals and who forgot to lock the door, and somehow it is the most gripping television you will watch all month.

For NRIs, the show functions as something close to emotional time travel. The textures are so specific — the steel almirah, the one good sofa reserved for guests, the passive-aggressive chai offerings — that watching from a living room in New Jersey or Mississauga can feel physically disorienting. You are there. You are home. And then the episode ends, and you are not. This connection to home is particularly poignant for the Indian diaspora, as it evokes memories of family gatherings and cultural traditions that may feel distant yet remain deeply ingrained.

Moreover, the themes of family, aspirations, and the bittersweet nature of growing up resonate with many NRIs who navigate the complexities of maintaining ties with their roots while building new lives abroad. The show subtly reflects the challenges of remittances, the emotional weight of dual citizenship, and the longing for familial bonds that often transcend borders.

Season 5 is streaming now on **SonyLIV**, with new episodes dropping weekly. Episode 3 arrives on **June 12**. The season runs five episodes total, directed by **Abhay Raut** and creator **Shreyansh Pandey**, with writing by **Vidit Tripathi**.

If you have not watched Gullak before, start from Season 1. If you have, you already know what you are doing this weekend. Grab the remote, pour the chai, and let the Mishras remind you what home sounds like.
